boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Bentley University
boards.description: Bentley students balance rigorous business studies with a late-night food scene that spans on-campus staples and the diverse 'Restaurant Row' of Moody Street.

cards.title: Harry's Pub
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Late Night Hub
cards.notes: Visit the Student Center for bar-style food starting at 8:00 PM. It is the primary on-campus destination for students after the main dining hall closes.
cards.short_summary: The central on-campus spot for late-night food and socializing in the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Harry's Pub offers food service nightly starting at 8:00 PM, with regular hours until 12:45 AM Sunday-Thursday and 1:45 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:45 AM (Sun-Thu) and 1:45 AM (Fri-Sat) during the academic year.

cards.title: Margaritas Mexican Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Moody Street Late Night Fiesta
cards.notes: Head to Moody Street for late-night appetizers and a lively atmosphere. It is a popular off-campus choice for students using the Falcon Flyer shuttle.
cards.short_summary: A staple of Waltham's Restaurant Row offering late-night food and a dedicated 'Late Night Fiesta' menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Margaritas in Waltham is open until 12:00 AM on Tuesday-Wednesday and 1:00 AM Thursday-Saturday, with a late-night menu available from 9:00 PM to close.
cards.source_title: Margaritas Mexican Restaurant in Waltham MA
cards.access_notes: Kitchen and bar open until 1:00 AM on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.

cards.title: In A Pickle Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Brunch and Late Night Smash Burgers
cards.notes: Try the 'Night Menu' featuring smash burgers and wings. This Moody Street favorite is known for creative comfort food and large portions.
cards.short_summary: A famous Waltham eatery that extends its creative menu into the late evening with a dedicated night selection.
cards.evidence_claim: In A Pickle offers a 'Night Menu' served from 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM Wednesday through Saturday, including wings and smash burgers.
cards.source_title: In A Pickle Restaurant - Contact Us
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Wednesday through Saturday.

cards.title: Shopper's Café
cards.subtitle: Neighborhood Pub with Late Kitchen
cards.notes: Grab a burger or steak tips at this family-owned spot. The kitchen stays open later than many other local restaurants on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Waltham neighborhood pub known for its late-night kitchen and sports-friendly atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Shopper's Café kitchen is open until 11:00 PM Thursday through Saturday, with the bar remaining open until 1:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Kitchen open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Bistro 781
cards.subtitle: Elevated Late Night Dining
cards.notes: Enjoy a more upscale late-night meal on Moody Street. The name pays homage to the local area code and serves as a community gathering point.
cards.short_summary: An elevated American bistro on Moody Street that keeps its kitchen open until 11:00 PM on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Bistro 781 serves dinner until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday, with the bar closing later.
cards.access_notes: Dinner service available until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: Tessie's Bar & Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Craft Burgers on Main Street
cards.notes: Located on Main Street, this spot is known for creative burgers and a kitchen that serves until 11:00 PM on busy weekend nights.
cards.short_summary: A popular local spot for craft burgers and salads with extended kitchen hours on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Tessie's Bar & Kitchen in Waltham keeps its kitchen open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Kitchen open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Pini's Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: Late Night Pizza Delivery
cards.notes: A go-to for pizza delivery or pickup. While not open past midnight, it remains a consistent evening option for students in dorms.
cards.short_summary: A local favorite for thin-crust pizza and Italian subs, frequently ordered by the Bentley community.
cards.evidence_claim: Pini's Pizzeria in Waltham is open until 9:00 PM daily, serving as a reliable evening meal option.
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM daily for pickup and delivery.

cards.title: Bentley University Library
cards.subtitle: Midnight Study Sessions
cards.notes: The library provides a quiet space for late-night academic work, with hours extending to midnight for much of the week.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic hub for late-night study, offering extended hours during the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bentley University Library is open until 12:00 AM Sunday through Thursday during the academic trimester.
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM Sunday-Thursday; hours may extend to 24/7 during final exams.

cards.title: Waltham Falcon Flyer
cards.subtitle: The Late Night Connection
cards.notes: Use the university shuttle to reach Moody Street restaurants. It is the essential link between campus and Waltham's dining scene.
cards.short_summary: The university's shuttle service that connects students to off-campus dining and transportation hubs late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Falcon Flyer shuttle operates until 11:38 PM on Fridays and 11:47 PM on Saturdays, with stops at Moody Street.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Routes and Schedules - Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Operates until approximately 11:45 PM on weekends during the academic year.

cards.title: The Nest
cards.subtitle: Retail Dining Option
cards.notes: Located in the Student Center, this retail spot offers meal trade options and quick bites for students studying late.
cards.short_summary: A retail dining location on campus providing flexible meal options beyond the traditional dining hall hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nest is listed as a designated retail location for meal trades and is located within the Student Center hub.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by semester; typically open for evening retail service.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study zones, specialized labs, and quiet corners that Bentley students use to navigate their rigorous business curriculum and collaborative projects.

cards.title: The Back Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library Upper and Main Levels
cards.notes: Head to the back reading rooms on the main and upper floors for near-total silence. These designated Red Zones are strictly for focused, individual work without distraction.
cards.short_summary: Strictly silent study areas located in the rear of the library's main and upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates the back reading rooms on the main and upper levels as Silent Study Zones (Red Zones) for students who prefer an almost silent environment.
cards.access_notes: Open during library operating hours; accessible to all students with a valid ID.

cards.title: Collaborative Work at The Bubble
cards.subtitle: Student Center Third Floor
cards.notes: Utilize the long tables and high-top seating for group projects. It offers a lively atmosphere where you can stay productive while remaining connected to the campus hub.
cards.short_summary: A popular collaborative study area on the top floor of the Student Center with ample outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bubble is a well-known study spot on the top floor of the Student Center featuring long tables, high-top seating, and charging stations.
cards.access_notes: Located on the 3rd floor; open during Student Center hours.

cards.title: The Trading Room
cards.subtitle: Smith Academic Technology Center 226
cards.notes: Access 24 Bloomberg terminals and real-time financial data. This high-tech lab is the go-to spot for finance majors to practice market analysis and portfolio management.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art investment research center with 60 workstations and Bloomberg terminals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Trading Room features 60 workstations and 24 Bloomberg terminals for investment research and financial technology training.
cards.source_title: Trading Room (Hughey Center for Financial Services) | Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Smith; check lab hours for open access.

cards.title: Quiet Reading in the Bowles Room
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library Lower Level
cards.notes: Find a quiet nook among the 2,600-volume personal library of Edward Bowles. It is an ideal spot for hushed reading or using the dedicated video viewing stations.
cards.short_summary: A quiet lower-level room housing a donated book collection and video viewing equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowles Room on the lower level contains a 2,600-volume collection and 8 stations for viewing VHS or DVD content.
cards.access_notes: Designated as a Quiet Study Zone (Orange Zone) where hushed conversation is permitted.

cards.title: The Orange Chair Nooks
cards.subtitle: Morison Hall End Corridors
cards.notes: Seek out the quiet hallways at the end of Morison Hall. These nooks with orange chairs offer a secluded alternative to the library during busy finals weeks.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, lesser-known study spaces with orange chairs located at the ends of Morison Hall corridors.
cards.evidence_claim: Morison Hall contains study spaces with orange chairs and glass-encased study rooms that are known by students as quiet spots for finals.
cards.source_title: Best Hidden Places to Study Around Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours; limited seating available.

cards.title: The CIS Sandbox
cards.subtitle: Smith Academic Technology Center 234
cards.notes: Collaborate on tech projects in this social learning space. It is staffed by peer tutors who can help with IT and computer information systems coursework.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative technology learning lab and social space for CIS students.
cards.evidence_claim: The CIS Sandbox is a learning lab where students work on technology projects and receive peer support.
cards.access_notes: Located in Smith 234; open to all students during lab hours.

cards.title: Jennison Hall Collaboratories
cards.subtitle: Jennison Hall Floors 2-4
cards.notes: Use the movable tablet desks and integrated technology for group brainstorming. These modern rooms are designed for flexible, interactive team sessions.
cards.short_summary: Modernized classrooms in Jennison Hall equipped with mobile furniture and collaborative tech.
cards.evidence_claim: Jennison Hall features active learning classrooms with tablet desks on casters and collaboratory rooms with shared displays.
cards.access_notes: Available for student use when classes are not in session.

cards.title: The MCC Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Center Level 2
cards.notes: Recharge in this student-designed space. It serves as a comfortable community hub for connection and quiet study between classes.
cards.short_summary: A recently renovated lounge in the Student Center providing a space for community and study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claudette Blot Multicultural Center Lounge was redesigned by students to create a space for community members to recharge and connect.
cards.source_title: Bentley Unveils Newly Renovated Multicultural Center Lounge
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the Student Center.

cards.title: Adamian Corner Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Adamian Academic Center Third Floor
cards.notes: Find the large study room on the third floor for ample table space and natural light. It is often quieter than central campus spots due to its peripheral location.
cards.short_summary: Spacious study rooms in the Adamian Academic Center known for natural light and quiet.
cards.evidence_claim: The Adamian Academic Center contains a large study room on the third floor and smaller rooms near the parking lot side that offer natural light and quiet.
cards.source_title: Best Hidden Places to Study Around Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; check for room availability on the third floor.

cards.title: The HUSH Pod
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library
cards.notes: Book this single-occupancy soundproof pod for Zoom interviews or hybrid classes. It provides a private, quiet environment within the library's open floors.
cards.short_summary: A single-occupancy soundproof acoustic room for private calls and focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: The library features a HUSH Pod, which is a single-occupancy soundproof space for hybrid classes or interviews.
cards.source_title: Hush Pod Acoustic Room | Bentley University Library
cards.access_notes: Available for student and staff use; check library for reservation details.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best free social spaces and activities at Bentley University, from high-tech learning labs to quiet campus greens.

cards.title: Relax in the Living Room
cards.subtitle: Bentley Student Center
cards.notes: Visit the first floor for pool and ping pong tables. You can rent equipment for free at the third-floor Business Center with your student ID.
cards.short_summary: A central social hub with free games and lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Living Room contains pool and ping pong tables, with free equipment rentals from the Business Center.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during Student Center hours; equipment requires Bentley ID.

cards.title: Browse the RSM Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library
cards.notes: Located at the library entrance, this gallery features six rotating exhibits annually by New England artists and is open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A free public art space located within the main university library.
cards.evidence_claim: The RSM Art Gallery is free and open to the public when the library is open.
cards.source_title: RSM Art Gallery at the Bentley Library
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; accessible to the general public.

cards.title: Ride the Harvard Shuttle
cards.subtitle: Campus Transportation
cards.notes: Board the shuttle at the Student Center for a free ride to Harvard Square. Remember to bring your Bentley ID for boarding.
cards.short_summary: Free transportation for students between campus and Cambridge.
cards.evidence_claim: All Bentley Shuttles are free. You must show a Bentley ID when boarding.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Routes and Schedules - Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Bentley ID; runs daily with reduced weekend hours.

cards.title: Workout at the Dana Center
cards.subtitle: Lower Campus
cards.notes: Access two floors of cardio and endurance equipment. The 10,000-square-foot fitness room is open to all current students.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus fitness facility for student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dana Center Gym is available to students, staff, and faculty and features a 10,000-square foot fitness/weight room.
cards.access_notes: Bentley ID card required for entry.

cards.title: Study in a Library Pod
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library
cards.notes: Choose from individual study carrels, cozy pods, or collaborative zones. Group rooms can be reserved for free via the EMS system.
cards.short_summary: Diverse quiet and collaborative study environments.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley Library offers a variety of study spaces including individual study carrels, cozy study pods, and 22 collaborative study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; some zones are designated for silent study.

cards.title: Explore the Trading Room
cards.subtitle: Smith Academic Technology Center
cards.notes: Visit this high-tech lab to use Bloomberg terminals and real-time financial data. It is open for student research outside of class times.
cards.short_summary: A world-class financial lab with professional-grade tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Trading Room features 60 workstations and 24 Bloomberg terminals available for student use.
cards.source_title: Trading Room (Hughey Center for Financial Services)
cards.access_notes: Available to students when not in use for scheduled classes.

cards.title: Hang Out on the Green
cards.subtitle: Upper Campus
cards.notes: This central lawn is the primary spot for outdoor socializing, sunbathing, and campus-wide events like Earthfest.
cards.short_summary: The central outdoor gathering spot on the upper campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Campus Green Space is a designated outdoor space used for events and student gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor area.

cards.entity_name: Center for Languages and International Collaboration (CLIC)
cards.title: Visit the CLIC Lab
cards.subtitle: Adamian Academic Center
cards.notes: Use this multipurpose space for language practice and cultural exchange. It offers specialized software and a collaborative atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative space for language learning and international culture.
cards.evidence_claim: CLIC is a multipurpose collaborative space that fosters communication across languages and cultures.
cards.source_title: Learning Labs: Where Learning Meets Technology | Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Open to all students during lab hours.

cards.title: Tune Your Bike for Free
cards.subtitle: Campus Amenities
cards.notes: Use the Dero Fix-it station to perform basic repairs. It includes tools and an air pump for public use near the campus bike racks.
cards.short_summary: A self-service station for free bicycle maintenance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dero Bike Fix-it station includes all tools necessary for basic repairs and is available for the community.
cards.access_notes: Available 24/7 for public use.

cards.title: Find Quiet in the Sacred Space
cards.subtitle: Student Center
cards.notes: Located on the lower level, this room is available for prayer, meditation, or quiet reflection away from the busy campus life.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room for spiritual and personal reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sacred Space in the Student Center provides a quiet space for prayer and reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students during Student Center hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From silent reading rooms to high-tech collaborative labs, Bentley University offers a range of environments tailored for business-focused research and group projects.

cards.title: Silent Study Zones
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library, Main and Upper Levels
cards.notes: Head to the back reading rooms on the main and upper floors for a strictly silent environment. Silence all devices and use headphones to maintain the quiet atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: Designated silent areas located in the back reading rooms of the library's main and upper levels.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates the back reading rooms on the main and upper levels as Silent Study Zones where almost no noise is expected.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; specific zones are marked with red signage for silence.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library, All Levels
cards.notes: Reserve one of 22 rooms online via the EMS system for group work. Most rooms feature LCD displays that connect to laptops for shared viewing.
cards.short_summary: Tech-equipped rooms for group collaboration, reservable by students for up to two hours per day.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley Library offers 22 collaborative study spaces across three levels, most featuring LCD displays or SMART boards, reservable via EMS.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via EMS; 15-minute check-in window applies.

cards.title: The Bubble
cards.subtitle: Student Center, Third Floor
cards.notes: Study at large tables or high-tops in this lively third-floor space. It offers a view of the living room below and is ideal for those who prefer background noise.
cards.short_summary: A popular, high-energy study area on the third floor of the Student Center overlooking the main lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bubble is a designated study area on the third floor of the Student Center featuring large tables and high-top seating.
cards.source_title: My Favorite Study Spots on Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; no reservation required for open seating.

cards.title: Deloitte Café
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library, Main Level
cards.notes: Grab a bagel and find a seat in this collaborative zone. It is a social study spot where conversation is welcome and food is easily accessible.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative study area located within the library's main level cafe, allowing for conversation and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Deloitte Café (Einstein's) is located on the main level of the library and is designated as a Collaborative Study Zone.
cards.access_notes: Open during library and cafe operating hours.

cards.title: Morison Study Nooks
cards.subtitle: Morison Hall, End of Hallway
cards.notes: Look for the orange chairs at the end of the hallway past the CMT. These nooks offer a quiet, secluded alternative to the main campus hubs.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, lesser-known study alcoves featuring distinctive orange seating located in Morison Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Morison Hall contains study nooks with orange chairs at the end of the hallways that are noted for being quiet and less crowded.
cards.source_title: Best Hidden Places to Study Around Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: Adamian Study Room
cards.subtitle: Adamian Academic Center, Near Parking Lots
cards.notes: Find this room at the end of the building for a space with comfortable chairs and large tables. It benefits from significant natural light and low foot traffic.
cards.short_summary: A bright and quiet study room located at the edge of the Adamian Academic Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Adamian Academic Center features a small study room at the end of the building known for natural light and a quiet atmosphere.
cards.source_title: Best Hidden Places to Study Around Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically used for individual or small group work.

cards.title: LaCava Center Booths
cards.subtitle: LaCava Center, Dining Area
cards.notes: Utilize the booths in LaCava for a mix of dining and studying. These spots include power outlets, making them convenient for long sessions between classes.
cards.short_summary: Dining booths equipped with power outlets, suitable for casual studying and meals.
cards.evidence_claim: LaCava Center features booths with outlets that students use for studying between classes.
cards.source_title: My Favorite Study Spots on Campus
cards.access_notes: Available during LaCava Center operating hours.

cards.title: Smith ATC Collaboratory
cards.subtitle: Smith Academic Technology Center
cards.notes: Work in small groups at stations featuring 50-inch displays and PC setups. These rooms are designed specifically for technology-infused collaborative learning.
cards.short_summary: High-tech group workstations in the Smith Center designed for collaborative digital projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Smith Academic Technology Center houses collaboratory classrooms (e.g., Smith 210, 212) with 6-person workstations and 50-inch displays.
cards.access_notes: Available for student use when not reserved for classes.

cards.title: The Bowles Room
cards.subtitle: Bentley Library, Lower Level
cards.notes: Study among a collection of 2,600 volumes in this lower-level room. It is designated as a Quiet Study Zone, allowing for light ambient noise.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study room on the library's lower level housing a specialized book collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowles Room on the lower level of the library is a designated Quiet Study Zone and houses a donated collection of 2,600 volumes.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; designated as an orange Quiet Study Zone.

cards.title: Jennison Active Learning Spaces
cards.subtitle: Jennison Hall, Multiple Floors
cards.notes: Use the mobile tablet desks on casters to quickly configure a group study setup. These renovated spaces offer a modern, bright environment for academic work.
cards.short_summary: Modernized classrooms in Jennison Hall with flexible furniture for group or individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Jennison Hall features active learning classrooms equipped with tablet desks on casters for easy mobility and group setup.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours when classes are not in session.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Bentley University, from the vibrant dining scene on Moody Street to the convenient retail hubs along Lexington Street.

cards.title: The Dining Corridor
cards.subtitle: Moody Street, Waltham
cards.notes: Walk this vibrant stretch to find diverse international cuisine and local favorites like Bison County, serving as the primary social hub for off-campus student dining.
cards.short_summary: Waltham's primary dining and social district located south of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Moody Street is described as the 'hot spot for foodies' and a vibrant social scene for Bentley students, featuring restaurants like Bison County and Margaritas.
cards.source_title: 39 Places That Prove Waltham Has Everything You Need - Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Bentley shuttle or a short drive; most businesses are open daily until 9:00 PM or later.

cards.title: The Essentials Block
cards.subtitle: Lexington Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this retail block for daily necessities at Star Market and quick bites at Panera Bread or Chipotle, conveniently located just north of the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A major shopping center on Lexington Street providing student essentials.
cards.evidence_claim: Waltham Plaza at 1074 Lexington Street features Star Market, Panera Bread, and Chipotle, serving as a local stop for everyday essentials.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; Star Market typically operates 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

cards.title: The Civic Heart
cards.subtitle: Main Street at Elm Street
cards.notes: Attend seasonal community festivals or enjoy the open green space at this central park, which serves as the anchor for Waltham's historic downtown district.
cards.short_summary: A central public park and gathering space in downtown Waltham.
cards.evidence_claim: Waltham Common is a recognized place near Bentley University used for community events and public transit connections.
cards.source_title: How to Get to Bentley University in Waltham by Bus, Train or Subway?
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Campus Connector
cards.subtitle: Beaver Street Corridor
cards.notes: Travel this scenic route connecting the main campus to the Lyman Estate and local recreation areas, passing through the historic DeVincent Farm area.
cards.short_summary: A key thoroughfare bordering the southern edge of Bentley's campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Beaver Street proceeds eastward past Forest Street and Bentley University, connecting Lexington Street to the Lyman Estate area.
cards.access_notes: Public roadway with sidewalks; provides access to Bentley's Lewis Lot.

cards.title: The Recreation Block
cards.subtitle: Trapelo Road Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this newly developed 120-acre recreation area for walking paths, adult fitness stations, and open field space just north of the university.
cards.short_summary: A large municipal recreation area on Trapelo Road near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Waltham opened a 120-acre recreation area at 200 Trapelo Road in 2025, featuring walking paths and fitness areas.
cards.access_notes: Open 7 days a week from 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM; no street parking allowed.

cards.title: The Skyline View
cards.subtitle: Totten Pond Road
cards.notes: Hike the trails at this park to reach one of the highest points in the region, offering panoramic views of the Boston skyline and surrounding suburbs.
cards.short_summary: A major wooded park on Totten Pond Road known for its hiking and views.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Hill Park at 314 Totten Pond Road is a primary location for outdoor recreation and city-run programs.
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily; main entrance is located on Totten Pond Road.

cards.title: The Student Residential Block
cards.subtitle: Linden Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this corridor known for off-campus student housing options and its proximity to the shops and restaurants of Main Street.
cards.short_summary: A residential street popular for off-campus student apartments.
cards.evidence_claim: Linden Street is noted for having housing options near Bentley University and is located about a mile from the Main Street downtown district.
cards.source_title: Linden Street Apartments - 99-109 Linden St Waltham, MA 02452
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; parking may be restricted to residents with permits.

cards.title: The Retail Hub
cards.subtitle: Lexington Street at Lakeview
cards.notes: Shop for apparel and home goods at T.J. Maxx or find unique gifts at The Paper Store in this busy retail hub north of campus.
cards.short_summary: A retail center on Lexington Street featuring national brands.
cards.evidence_claim: Wal-Lex Shopping Center at 850 Lexington Street includes T.J. Maxx and The Paper Store, serving as a retail hub in Waltham.
cards.source_title: Discover the Vibrant Wal-Lex Shopping Center - Evendo
cards.access_notes: Open daily; typical hours are 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM Monday through Saturday.

cards.title: The Fitness Corridor
cards.subtitle: Route 60 Corridor
cards.notes: Find specialized fitness facilities like the Waverley Oaks Athletic Club and local eateries along this road connecting Waltham to Belmont.
cards.short_summary: A commercial and fitness-oriented corridor east of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Waverley Oaks Road (Route 60) features businesses like the Waverley Oaks Athletic Club and City Streets Restaurant.
cards.source_title: Businesses in Waltham, MA - Enigma Data
cards.access_notes: Public roadway; businesses have varying hours.

cards.title: The Academic Link
cards.subtitle: Forest Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this primary campus thoroughfare to reach the North Campus residential buildings and the main university entrance from Trapelo Road.
cards.short_summary: The main street running through and connecting Bentley's campus areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Forest Street is the location of the main Bentley campus entrance and connects to the North Campus residential buildings.
cards.access_notes: Public street with university shuttle stops and pedestrian sidewalks.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From late-night pancake feasts served by faculty to the historic Falcon Walk, these traditions define the Bentley University experience in Waltham.

cards.title: Spring Day
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate End-of-Year Celebration
cards.notes: Join thousands of students for a day of food trucks, inflatables, and a major headliner concert at the Bentley Arena before spring finals begin.
cards.short_summary: An annual end-of-semester festival featuring carnival activities and a high-profile concert organized by the Campus Activities Board.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Day is a popular annual end-of-semester event held each year the weekend before spring finals, featuring food trucks and a headliner concert.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Open to current Bentley students; wristbands are required for entry to the concert and main activities.

cards.title: Breakfast by Moonlight
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: Head to the dining hall during finals week to be served pancakes and tater tots by university faculty and staff in this late-night tradition.
cards.short_summary: A late-night breakfast event where faculty and staff serve students during finals week to provide a study break and sustenance.
cards.evidence_claim: Before final exams begin, Bentley's faculty and staff serve a delicious late-night breakfast to students called Breakfast by Moonlight.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Typically held late at night (around 10:00 PM or later) in the 921 Dining Hall during finals week.

cards.title: Falcon Walk
cards.subtitle: The First March to Convocation
cards.notes: Follow Flex the Falcon and the orientation leaders in a spirited procession across campus to mark the official start of your academic journey.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial walk for new students led by the mascot and orientation leaders, leading into the annual Convocation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley's incoming class is led by the Flex the Falcon mascot during the Falcon Walk tradition as part of orientation.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late August or early September during New Student Orientation.

cards.title: Super Bingo
cards.subtitle: High-Stakes Campus Competition
cards.notes: Compete for major prizes like flat-screen TVs and designer tech in this high-energy event that often features pajama-themed nights.
cards.short_summary: A massive, high-energy bingo event attended by over 1,000 students, known for its significant prizes and themed atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: About 1,000 students typically show up for Super Bingo, a high-energy Bentley tradition with themes like pajama night and prizes like flat-screen TVs.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Held periodically throughout the year in the Bentley Arena or Dana Center.

cards.title: Falcon Weekend
cards.subtitle: Homecoming and Family Reunion
cards.notes: Celebrate Bentley pride with a weekend of football, tailgating at Tailgate Village, and reunions for alumni and families.
cards.short_summary: The university's combined Homecoming, Family Weekend, and Reunion celebration held every fall.
cards.evidence_claim: Falcon Weekend is Bentley's homecoming, family weekend and reunions all wrapped into one, featuring a football game and Tailgate Village.
cards.access_notes: Events are spread across Upper and Lower campus; some specific events require registration or tickets.

cards.title: MLK Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A Legacy of Celebration
cards.notes: Attend this longstanding January tradition that honors Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. through speakers, performances, and community reflection.
cards.short_summary: A tradition dating back to 1986 that has evolved from a dinner into a full day of celebration and learning centered on MLK's principles.
cards.evidence_claim: The MLK Breakfast tradition goes back to 1986 and has evolved into a full day of interactive sessions connected to Dr. King's principles.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Held annually in January; often a sold-out event requiring advance registration.

cards.title: Senior Toast
cards.subtitle: A Final Salute on the President's Lawn
cards.notes: Gather on the President's lawn before graduation to receive a commemorative champagne flute and toast to your four years at Bentley.
cards.short_summary: A formal toast for graduating seniors held on the university president's lawn during Senior Week.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Toast is a tradition on the President's lawn where seniors receive a free champagne flute and toast to their four years.
cards.source_title: A Guide to All Things 'Senior' at Bentley
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to graduating seniors; registration is required in advance.

cards.title: Black United Body Fashion Show
cards.subtitle: Style and Culture on the Runway
cards.notes: Experience one of the most popular cultural events on campus, featuring student models and local designers in a high-production runway show.
cards.short_summary: An annual fashion show hosted by the Black United Body (BUB) that showcases culture and creativity.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Black United Body fashion show is a signature event that features local designers and student models.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Bentley Arena; tickets are required for attendance.

cards.title: The Rock near Slade Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Reflection Spot
cards.notes: Visit this natural landmark near Slade Hall, a favorite spot for students to gather late at night for deep conversations and stargazing.
cards.short_summary: A large rock formation near Slade Hall that serves as an informal gathering spot and a place for student reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The big rock near Slade Hall is a favorite hidden spot where students climb up late at night for conversations.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors near Slade Hall; accessible 24/7 to the campus community.

cards.title: Falcon Fest
cards.subtitle: Flex the Falcon's Birthday Bash
cards.notes: Celebrate the university mascot's birthday on September 30th with cake, games, and campus-wide festivities.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration held on September 30th to mark the birthday of Flex the Falcon, the university's mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: Flex's birthday is September 30 which is celebrated by students at an event called Falcon Fest.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or around September 30th, typically in the Student Center or on the greenspace.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Bentley University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential sequence of events and campus landmarks for new Falcons during their first weekend in Waltham.

cards.title: Arrive for Move-In
cards.subtitle: The First Stop for New Falcons
cards.notes: Start your journey at the Miller Parking Garage for check-in. Follow the staggered arrival times to ensure a smooth transition into your residence hall.
cards.short_summary: The primary check-in and arrival point for new students moving into Bentley residence halls.
cards.evidence_claim: New students are directed to the upper level of the Miller Parking Garage as their first stop for move-in and screening.
cards.source_title: Parents and Families Orientation - Waltham - Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to students with assigned move-in time slots during orientation weekend.

cards.title: Attend University Convocation
cards.subtitle: The Official Academic Start
cards.notes: Join your class for this formal ceremony where faculty in regalia welcome you. It marks the official beginning of your academic career as a Falcon.
cards.short_summary: A traditional ceremony held during orientation to officially welcome the new undergraduate class.
cards.evidence_claim: University Convocation is a Bentley tradition that marks the official start to the academic year for new students.
cards.access_notes: Required for all new undergraduate students; families are invited to attend.

cards.title: First Meal at The 921
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Dining Hall
cards.notes: Head to the Student Center for your first all-you-care-to-eat meal. It's the central hub for meeting floor-mates over breakfast or dinner.
cards.short_summary: Bentley's primary all-you-care-to-eat dining facility located within the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center is home to the 921 Dining Hall, Bentley's all-you-care-to-eat dining facility.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; check the Falcon Dining website for specific weekend hours.

cards.title: Relax in the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Billiards and Community Space
cards.notes: Take a break from unpacking to play a game of pool or relax in the 'Living Room' area. It's a great low-pressure way to meet other new students.
cards.short_summary: A social space in the Student Center featuring pool tables and lounge areas for student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can relax and play pool or seek out quiet spaces within the Student Center.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; game equipment can be rented at the 3rd-floor Business Center.

cards.title: Explore the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation Hub
cards.notes: Visit the 10,000-square foot fitness room to see the cardio and weight equipment. It's a popular spot for students to stay active between orientation events.
cards.short_summary: The main athletic facility on campus featuring a fitness center, pool, and basketball courts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dana Athletic Center features a 10,000-square foot fitness/weight room for students.
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Bentley ID for access; typically open 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Academic Resource Center
cards.notes: Walk through the library to find the group study rooms and 'Hush Pods.' Locating your preferred quiet zone early helps for the first week of classes.
cards.short_summary: The university's main library offering diverse study environments from collaborative rooms to quiet zones.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley Library offers a variety of study spaces including 22 collaborative study rooms and soundproof HUSH pods.
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 10:00 AM–12:00 AM; check website for specific orientation weekend hours.

cards.title: Ride the Shuttle to Cambridge
cards.subtitle: Off-Campus Exploration
cards.notes: Catch the shuttle from the LaCava Center to Harvard Square. It's a free way to explore the local area and access the MBTA Red Line into Boston.
cards.short_summary: A university-provided shuttle service connecting the Bentley campus to Harvard Square in Cambridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harvard Shuttle departs Bentley on the half-hour and provides access to Cambridge and MBTA services.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Routes and Schedules - Bentley University
cards.access_notes: Weekend service typically starts at 10:30 AM from Bentley; valid student ID may be required.

cards.title: Explore Moody Street
cards.subtitle: Local Waltham Shuttle
cards.notes: Use the Falcon Flyer shuttle to visit Moody Street's shops and restaurants. It's the easiest way to get to the grocery store or local cafes.
cards.short_summary: A shuttle route serving the Waltham area, including Moody Street and the Commuter Rail station.
cards.evidence_claim: The Falcon Flyer provides access to Moody St shops, restaurants, and Hannaford's Supermarket.
cards.access_notes: Saturday service runs from 10:45 AM to 11:47 PM; Sunday service ends at 10:17 PM.

cards.title: Visit the Bentley Arena
cards.subtitle: Home of Falcon Hockey
cards.notes: Check out the LEED Platinum-certified ice arena. Even if there isn't a game, it's a landmark building where students gather for major events.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art ice arena that hosts Bentley's Division I hockey program and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bentley Arena is the first standalone ice arena in the country to receive LEED platinum certification.
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled events and games; check the athletics calendar for weekend activities.

cards.title: Join a Student Organization
cards.subtitle: Get Involved on Campus
cards.notes: Look for the bi-annual Activities Fair usually held early in the semester. It's the best time to explore over 100 clubs and find your community.
cards.short_summary: An event where student organizations showcase their activities to recruit new members.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley has over 100 clubs and organizations and the bi-annual Activities Fair highlights them all.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Student Center or on the campus green; check orientation schedule for exact timing.
